reviews.reason: Binding an integer to an opaque PostgreSQL statement is private DB2 execution state; typed operations carry validated integer fields and bind them inside the owner process.
Binding a 64-bit value to a process-owned statement cannot cross the bus; bounded request fields are decoded and bound wholly inside DB2.
Statement text binding exposes an opaque handle and unbounded database plumbing; each wire operation validates bounded strings before DB2 performs its own bind.
Reading a double from an opaque result cursor is private row decoding; DB2 validates and encodes the domain value into a bounded typed reply.
Reading an integer from a process-owned result cursor cannot be remote API; complete operations decode rows and return explicit domain fields.
Reading a 64-bit column is local cursor traversal; DB2 owns the result lifetime and emits only the bounded typed domain value.
A borrowed text pointer into PostgreSQL result storage is process-local lifetime state; DB2 copies validated bounded text into operation replies before finalizing.
Transporting caller-supplied raw SQL would violate the DB2 ownership and schema boundary; every bus mutation names a declared operation with DB2-owned SQL.
Finalizing an opaque statement is local lifetime cleanup; DB2 releases all query resources before returning any operation reply.
Preparing caller-provided SQL and returning an opaque statement handle cannot cross a process boundary; declared operations prepare private fixed SQL inside DB2.
Incremental cursor stepping would create a chatty handle protocol; DB2 exhausts or bounds the result set and returns one complete structured reply.
Affected-row inspection belongs to the private statement lifetime; a mutation operation maps it to bounded domain evidence before replying.
Installing the bounded fork/exec capture capability is private immutable process bootstrap; no callback pointer or command-execution surface crosses the event bus.
A PostgreSQL connection is private process state and cannot cross the bus; each caller is replaced by a bounded operation that owns its complete transaction inside DB2.

The typed lifecycle.dimension_reset operation keeps schema replacement, maintenance marking, and requeue accounting inside one DB2-owned operator transaction while returning only bounded structured evidence.
The typed lifecycle.embedder_serving_id operation replaces the curator replay direct caller with DB2's bounded effective vector-space identity; empty remains the legacy no-identity state.
The typed lifecycle.embedding_dimension operation replaces production direct callers; the effective pgvector schema width remains DB2 authority.
The typed lifecycle.embedding_refusals operation replaces the KB health direct caller; the rejected width is DB2 pgvector diagnostic evidence.
The typed lifecycle.embedding_refusals operation replaces the KB health direct caller; refusal count is DB2 pgvector diagnostic evidence.
The typed lifecycle.health operation replaces production direct callers; PostgreSQL schema and extension readiness remain DB2 authority.
Database opening, schema application, and pool construction are private process bootstrap; the supervisor starts DB2 before exposing any bus capability.
The typed lifecycle.health operation proves the DB2 owner is initialized before reporting PostgreSQL and canonical KB readiness.
The typed lifecycle.health operation exposes canonical KB-table readiness together with the schema probe; that evidence remains DB2 authority.
The cJSON response builder is a process-local compatibility facade; the learning proposal lookup becomes a bounded typed operation and JSON presentation remains with its caller.
The cJSON list adapter cannot cross the typed bus; a bounded learning list operation returns fixed proposal records while the caller owns JSON serialization.
The legacy cJSON mutation wrapper is retired at the process boundary; DB2 performs rejection and returns the bounded typed proposal before any caller-specific JSON encoding.
The cJSON scene-list facade is process-local presentation code; the existing fixed scene rows define a bounded memory operation reply instead.
The cJSON scene-member facade stays out of the transport contract; DB2 returns a bounded array of fixed member records and the caller renders JSON.
Beginning a caller-held content transaction cannot cross the module boundary; each document, PDF, or code-index mutation becomes one bounded operation with DB2-owned atomicity.
Caller-controlled content commits are private DB2 mechanics; a complete index-family mutation commits before returning its structured reply and never exposes a transaction token.
Content transaction rollback stays inside DB2; failed, denied, or cancelled composite index operations roll back before returning and cannot leave caller-owned database state.
Lease scope terminates process-local PostgreSQL ownership and has no wire representation; it disappears when the enclosing DB2 work becomes one bounded request.
Idle-lease release is process-local pool hygiene, not a remote database operation; the standalone owner releases its own leases between complete bus requests.

Applying transaction-local PostgreSQL maintenance context is private DB2 execution state; each maintenance wire operation carries its bounded worker and project scope and owns the complete transaction.
The thread-local maintenance job binding cannot cross a process boundary; generated operations carry the named worker and bounded project on every complete DB2 request.
Clearing a process-local maintenance job binding has no wire representation; explicit request scope replaces the caller-owned thread-local lifetime.
Beginning a PostgreSQL transaction from thread-local maintenance state is private DB2 execution; a typed operation validates explicit scope and begins its own transaction instead.
A caller-controlled commit is forbidden across the module boundary; each declared maintenance mutation commits before publishing its bounded reply.
A caller-controlled rollback is process-local transaction cleanup; failed or cancelled maintenance operations roll back inside DB2 before returning transport status.
Releasing process-owned export buffers is local lifetime management; the memory export operation encodes bounded rows into its reply and frees every allocation before returning.
Clearing thread-local memory query context has no wire representation; each bounded memory request carries its scope and DB2 discards that request-local state before replying.
Reading process thread-local scope is private memory-operation plumbing; explicit bounded scope fields replace implicit caller-owned state across the bus.
Per-candidate rank probes would expose chatty implicit state; DB2 applies scope ranking inside the complete bounded memory search and returns only the ranked result set.
A setter for thread-local workspace and project scope cannot cross a process boundary; typed memory requests carry the bounded scope with the operation that consumes it.
A single-row scope-tag SQL probe is private DB2 query planning; complete memory search and retrieval operations enforce scope before returning bounded rows.
The legacy-workspace membership probe remains an internal compatibility predicate folded into scoped memory operations, not a separately callable bus capability.
The typed lifecycle.postgres_status operation replaces the doctor command's direct PostgreSQL diagnostics call with bounded availability and metric fields.
The typed lifecycle.pool_status operation replaces the production health caller; PostgreSQL pool occupancy and counters remain DB2 process authority.

The injected embedder callback is a process-local compatibility seam and cannot cross the bus; callers resolve the running endpoint's dimension before submitting the typed reset operation, which always carries an explicit target.
The typed lifecycle.reembed_clear_maintenance operation keeps the dimension-consistency check, optional force override, diagnostic snapshot, and marker delete inside one DB2 action.
The typed lifecycle.reembed_clear operation replaces the curator drain's direct maintenance-marker delete with an idempotent DB2 mutation.
The typed lifecycle.reembed_status operation replaces direct reads of the canonical maintenance marker while retaining DB2 schema and rebuild authority.
The configured model identity is injected into the DB2 owner before initialization; exposing a post-attachment setter would violate atomic activation.
The operator-pinned embedding width is private pre-initialization configuration; the bus exposes only the resolved effective dimension.
The descriptor-owned default width is injected during private module bootstrap and is immutable once the DB2 process attaches.
Pin precedence is private startup configuration consumed while DB2 establishes canonical schema authority; it is not a runtime mutation.
Pool capacity is fixed before DB2 initialization and remains private to the process owner; lifecycle.pool_status exposes the resulting bounded state.
Schema apply-versus-verify mode is a private bootstrap choice made before opening DB2 and cannot be changed through the serving bus.
Connection and pool teardown belongs to supervised process termination; callers cannot remotely shut down the required DB2 capability.
A caller-held tenant transaction cannot cross the bus; each tenancy or tenant-scoped operation carries bounded verifier-owned principal fields and owns context setup through completion.
Committing caller-owned tenant state is not a wire operation; a complete scoped DB2 request commits before its reply and never returns a transaction token.
Rollback and tenant-GUC clearing remain DB2 process cleanup; failures, cancellation, and denied scope roll back before the typed operation returns.
